extraction.name: CT-RATE
extraction.description: CT-RATE is a dataset comprising 25,692 non-contrast 3D chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from 21,304 unique patients. The dataset includes 50,188 reconstructed CT volumes (over 14.3 million 2D slices) paired with radiology reports. Each scan is accompanied by its corresponding radiology report with impression and findings sections. The dataset is enriched with 18 abnormality labels extracted from reports.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: CT-RATE consists of non-contrast chest CT volumes acquired between May 2015 and January 2023 from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. The dataset includes 50,188 reconstructed CT volumes from 25,692 distinct CT experiments conducted on 21,304 unique patients. CT volumes are reconstructed with various techniques for specific diagnostic requirements. Each CT exam is accompanied by a radiology report authored by a radiologist.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Non-contrast chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital acquired between May 2015 and January 2023. CT volumes were acquired using scanners from three different manufacturers: Philips (61.5%), Siemens (30.1%), and PNMS (8.4%).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: CT volumes are reconstructed using various techniques to suit different window settings. Each volume is resized to achieve uniform spacing of 0.75 mm in the x-axis and y-axis and 1.5 mm in the z-axis. Volumes are center-cropped or padded to reach a consistent resolution of 480×480×240. CT volumes are converted to Hounsfield Unit (HU) values using intercept and slope values from metadata. HU values are clipped to a range of -1000 to 1000 and normalized to a range of -1 to 1 during training.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing involves resizing volumes to uniform spacing (0.75 mm in x-y, 1.5 mm in z-axis), center-cropping or padding to 480×480×240 resolution, converting to Hounsfield Units using metadata intercept and slope values, clipping HU values to -1000 to 1000 range, and normalizing to -1 to 1 during training. Each volume's orientation is standardized by examining metadata. Quality control measures exclude volumes with contrast material or body parts other than chest.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multi-abnormality labels for 18 distinct abnormalities are extracted from radiology reports using an automated text classifier. 1,000 reports are manually annotated for 18 abnormalities by bilingual final-year medical students. A pretrained language model (RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m) is finetuned on these 1,000 annotated reports (80% training, 20% validation) to create an automated labeler. The finetuned model is then applied to classify the remaining 24,692 reports.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The finetuned RadBERT model's performance is evaluated using precision, recall, and F1 scores for each abnormality. Similar conditions are grouped together (e.g., left and right mucoid impactions under 'mucoid impaction', various lung opacities under 'lung opacity'). Conditions not referenced in either findings or impression sections are considered absent.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each report is annotated with 18 abnormality labels (multi-label classification)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Bilingual final-year medical students reviewed and corrected all translations and examined each report to remove personal information and ensure coherence.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m (pretrained language model finetuned for abnormality classification), Google Translate API (for translation), TotalSegmentator (for anatomical segmentation)
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes patient age (18-102 years, mean 48.8 years), sex distribution (41.6% female, 58.4% male), and geographic location (Istanbul, Turkey). All personal information is anonymized before release.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to address critical challenges in 3D medical imaging by enabling development of AI models that can assist radiologists, reduce workload, and potentially save lives in situations where immediate radiological expertise is not available. The open-source release democratizes access to 3D medical imaging data for research.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset originates from a single institution (Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital) in Turkey, which may introduce geographic and clinical setting biases that could limit generalizability to other populations. The dataset reflects real-world heterogeneity in CT scanners, acquisition protocols, and reconstruction techniques from a single center.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to chest CT volumes from a single institution in Turkey, which may affect generalizability. It does not include other 3D imaging modalities (MRI, PET) or other anatomical regions. The dataset lacks multi-abnormality segmentation and localization labels (planned for future work). Report quality and model performance remain insufficient for clinical deployment. The dataset reflects variability in radiologist writing styles and terminology.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training, validation, and testing of AI models for 3D medical imaging tasks including: multi-abnormality detection, case retrieval (volume-to-volume and report-to-volume), visual question answering, radiology report generation, and development of vision-language foundation models. The dataset is split into training (20,000 patients) and internal validation (1,304 patients) sets.
